retiredReason:
RETIRED — the entity was a DUPLICATE OF SMProfile-ProductionOrder, not a level above it.

(1) THE UPSTREAM SERVES ONE ROW, TWICE. Measured 2026-08-13 against sim-v5 PROD (.154), read-only: GET /api/orders and GET /api/customer-orders with the SAME query string (?exclude_status=CANCELLED,INVOICED,SHIPPED&limit=500) return BYTE-IDENTICAL bodies — identical md5 adbe865d603f1e27c562ae6054befb24, 665.809 bytes, 43 fields each, 500 rows each, identical key sets, and field-by-field across all 500 keys ZERO of the 43 fields differ. On every row the four id fields order_id, auftrag_nr, kundenauftrag_nr and production_order_no carry the SAME STRING. There is no field anywhere in the upstream that is a distinct customer-order number. This profile's identity (order_no <- kundenauftrag_nr) and SMProfile-ProductionOrder's identity (production_order_no) were therefore the same key wearing two names.

(2) WHAT THAT COST IN THE GRAPH, measured on .99 the same day. 48.486 nodes carry BOTH :CustomerOrder and :ProductionOrder — that is 100 % of :CustomerOrder; :CustomerOrder WITHOUT :ProductionOrder is 0, which is also why withdrawing this profile orphans nothing. TRIGGERS is 48.485 edges of which 48.485 are SELF-LOOPS and 0 join two distinct nodes: the L4->L3 chain 'customer demand triggers a manufacturing order' pointed every order at itself. The reverse edge TRIGGERED_BY has 0 edges and is removed from SMProfile-ProductionOrder in the same change. In the audit log the same duplication is 330.495 business_events under source erp-customer-orders over 46.031 distinct entity ids, of which 46.031 — every single one — are ALSO carried under erp-production-orders.

(3) THE MECHANISM WAS THIS FILE PLUS ITS SOURCE, NOT A SECOND WRITER. it-edge's buildKgSnapshot (services/it-edge/src/kg-snapshot.ts) emits one main object keyed on the source's idProperty and one STUB per declared edge, typed by the profile's relationship target. sources/rest/erp-customer-orders.json declared idProperty=kundenauftrag_nr and TRIGGERS(fkColumn=production_order_no, target ProductionOrder). Because those two columns hold the same string, every poll emitted {element_id: X, entity_type: 'CustomerOrder'} AND {element_id: X, entity_type: 'ProductionOrder'} plus a relationship X->X. kg-builder MERGEs on (id, owner) and SETs the label afterwards, so the two objects landed on ONE node wearing both labels. The duplication was self-inflicted by one declaration.

(4) WHY NOT TYPE-SCOPE THE ID INSTEAD. Namespacing the CustomerOrder id would have invented a distinction the data does not have: it would turn 48.486 visibly-conflicted nodes into ~46.031 pairs of content-identical nodes — an invisible duplication is worse than a visible conflict. The only option that establishes a real L4/L3 separation is for sim-v5 to serve genuine, separately-keyed customer orders; that is a data-model project against the live sim and is filed as a backlog item, not a fix.

(5) THE FILE STAYS. Its constraint order_overdue is a tombstone with 2.712 episodes still open in the KG, and discrepancy-engine resolves those episodes by constraint_defined_in='SMProfile-CustomerOrder'. Deleting the profile would make 2.712 standing findings unexplainable. The profile is retired, not deleted: nothing binds it (its source is withdrawn and erp-customer-orders is removed from it-edge SOURCE_IDS), so no :CustomerOrder node and no FOR_CUSTOMER/TRIGGERS edge can be created from it again.

(6) WHERE THE ATTRIBUTES WENT. order_no, customer_ref, customer_name, total_amount, currency, due_date and quantity are adopted by SMProfile-ProductionOrder v3.0.0 from the SAME upstream columns (kundenauftrag_nr, kunde_id, kunde_name, gesamtbetrag, waehrung, lieferdatum_soll, geplante_stueckzahl) via sources/rest/erp-production-orders.json v3.0.0, together with FOR_CUSTOMER and FOR_ARTICLE. This profile was the SOLE writer of customer_name (48.486 nodes) and of order_no on order entities, which is why the adoption is a precondition of the withdrawal and not a follow-up. unit_price is NOT adopted: it is declared here but /api/orders serves no such field and it is set on 0 nodes live, so the it-evaluator's quantity x unit_price fallback for total_amount has never once fired.

description: RETIRED 2026-08-13 (CAPT-ORDER) — see retiredReason. TOMBSTONE ONLY: nothing binds this profile, no node or edge can be created from it. Its commercial attributes and its FOR_CUSTOMER / FOR_ARTICLE edges are adopted by SMProfile-ProductionOrder v3.0.0. Kept because order_overdue below is a tombstone with 2.712 episodes still open in the KG that discrepancy-engine resolves by constraint_defined_in='SMProfile-CustomerOrder'. --- ORIGINAL: next/ v4 — Level-4 SALES order with a customer delivery commitment. Deliberately separated from the Level-3 OperationsRequest (ProductionOrder) it TRIGGERS: the sim currently conflates both onto one row (Sonderfall), but the clean MOM model keeps sales (L4) and production request/response (L3) apart. Plan-vs-actual deviations (late_delivery, qty_shortfall) are cross-entity OperationsRequest↔OperationsResponse checks and live in the cross-source phase, NOT here. Single-entity deviation: order_overdue (delivery commitment vs now).

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Ordered piece count of the order line (menge). Together with unit_price the source for total_amount — the real ERP does not keep an order total: order value = quantity × unit_price (derived by the it-evaluator).

attributes.name: unit_price
attributes.description: Unit price of the order line (stueckpreis). Together with quantity the source for total_amount (= quantity × unit_price).

attributes.name: total_amount
attributes.description: Order value. Delivered directly where available; otherwise derived by the it-evaluator as quantity × unit_price (the real ERP has no total column). Driver of the €-impact prioritization (expected_impact).

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: Customer delivery commitment (the promised date the sales order is due).

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Sales-order status, as it reaches THIS profile through OUR source binding. VOCABULARY MEASURED 2026-07-12 against the FULL population of sim-v5 PROD (.154) — all 47.513 customer orders, not a page and not the mapper's source code. /api/customer-orders is the SAME projection as /api/orders and carries exactly five raw statuses: CANCELLED 21.676 -> storniert, INVOICED 19.827 -> abgeschlossen, IN_PRODUCTION 4.305 -> in_arbeit, WAITING_PARTS 1.687 -> freigegeben, ON_HOLD 18 -> freigegeben. sources/rest/erp-customer-orders.json binds ?exclude_status=CANCELLED,INVOICED,SHIPPED, so 6.010 orders reach us and they carry exactly TWO values: in_arbeit and freigegeben. 'offen' (raw DRAFT|PROPOSED|PLANNED) and 'fertig' (raw PRODUCED|COMPLETED) DO NOT EXIST ANYWHERE IN THE ERP — 0 of 47.513 rows, filtered or not. This enum is therefore the COMPLETE image, not a snapshot lower bound. THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE OF order_overdue's RETIREMENT: its guard was `status eq 'offen'` — a value the source cannot produce. It has raised nothing since 2026-07-06 and CANNOT raise again. Note that an enum containing a fictional value makes ci/lint-vocabulary.mjs fake-green on exactly the guard it exists to catch; the gate is only as honest as the enum. Extend ONLY against a fresh measurement of the full population. --- 2026-08-03, THE ENUM NOW COMES FROM THE PRODUCER'S CONTRACT, NOT FROM A SAMPLE. Chasing observed values one at a time was Sisyphus: the declared set was [freigegeben, in_arbeit], a paginated count added fertig (12) and abgeschlossen (5), and while I was committing that, `offen` appeared once. A live population moves; a vocabulary declared from a sample of it is stale by construction. sim-v5 declares the CLOSED set itself — packages/api-erp/src/shapes.ts:96, 'canonical DE: offen|freigegeben|in_arbeit|fertig|abgeschlossen|storniert'. That is the authority, and it is what is declared here. storniert is DELIBERATELY OMITTED: it is status_raw CANCELLED, which the exclude_status filter this source sends (CANCELLED,INVOICED,SHIPPED) removes, so it cannot arrive through THIS binding. The other five can. Raw mapping measured on the live feed: IN_PRODUCTION -> in_arbeit, WAITING_PARTS + ON_HOLD -> freigegeben, COMPLETED -> fertig, DELIVERED -> abgeschlossen. HOW THE TWO-VALUE DECLARATION SURVIVED SINCE 2026-07-12: the endpoint caps a page at 5000 rows and the FIRST page carries only in_arbeit/freigegeben, so a single unpaginated request CONFIRMS the wrong answer. It caught me too. All values beyond in_arbeit/freigegeben are TERMINAL or pre-release and change no behaviour: every consumer treats only in_arbeit and freigegeben as running (golden-shift ACTIVE_STATUSES, run-builder order-tracker, it-evaluator recipe-band-resolver).

constraints.name: order_overdue
constraints.description: Open customer order past its due date (delivery delay against the customer commitment).
constraints.retiredReason:
RETIRED. The guard is structurally unsatisfiable: `when: status eq 'offen'` keys on a value this attribute CANNOT carry. Measured 2026-07-12 against the FULL population of sim-v5 PROD (.154) — all 47.513 customer orders, paginated (the endpoint caps a page at 500; a page is not a population).

(1) 'offen' DOES NOT EXIST. The ERP carries exactly five raw statuses — CANCELLED 21.676, INVOICED 19.827, IN_PRODUCTION 4.305, WAITING_PARTS 1.687, ON_HOLD 18 — and the projection maps them onto storniert / abgeschlossen / in_arbeit / freigegeben / freigegeben. 'offen' is emitted only for raw DRAFT|PROPOSED|PLANNED, and there is NOT ONE such row among all 47.513 (0,00 %). Our source binding (?exclude_status=CANCELLED,INVOICED,SHIPPED) narrows this further: 6.010 orders reach the profile and they carry exactly TWO values, in_arbeit and freigegeben. The guard therefore matches 0 of 6.010 — not 'rarely', but never, and not by accident of today's data: the raw state it needs does not exist in the system at all.

(2) IT HAS BEEN SILENT FOR SIX DAYS, AND THAT LOOKED LIKE HEALTH. Measured in the KG on .99: the newest order_overdue episode was raised 2026-07-06T10:02:21Z. Nothing since. It left 2.712 episodes standing open — raised under an EARLIER vocabulary, before the source began emitting the German canonical set — and those 2.712 have been sitting in the worklist as if they were live findings. A rule that cannot fire is indistinguishable from a factory with no overdue orders. That is the whole defect: a sleeping watchdog and a healthy factory look exactly the same from the outside.

(3) WHY IT WAS NOT SIMPLY REPAIRED. Swapping the literal to 'freigegeben'/'in_arbeit' would not restore the INTENT. The intent is 'an order that is still OPEN and past its promised date'. Both surviving values ARE open states, so the guard would degenerate to 'every order we can see', and the rule would then rest entirely on due_date >= $now. Whether that is a real promise is exactly what is NOT established: the ERP time axis is under repair (CAPT-ERP-TIME: 34.036 operations / 26 % end BEFORE their planned start, a backfill artifact). Re-pointing a dead guard at an unverified date field would convert 2.712 silent phantoms into a loud, continuously-firing lie. A quieter lie is not a truer one.

NOTE ON THE GUARD THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS: ci/lint-vocabulary.mjs checks guard literals against attributes[].enum. Until this same change, customer-order.status DECLARED an enum containing 'offen' (inherited from feat/ci-vocabulary-gate, which derived the enum from the projection's SOURCE CODE rather than from the data). Against that fictional enum the gate PASSED this guard — the vocabulary gate was fake-green on its own flagship case. The enum is corrected in this same commit. A gate is only as honest as the vocabulary it checks against.

Do NOT delete: the history is the evidence. Open customer order past its due date (delivery delay against the customer commitment).
